lines: Six digits, then you're riding, and Telo Ride remembers you for a year.
Type the code, paste it, or take the one your phone offers. Anything that isn't a digit drops away, and six digits confirm at once.
A code that doesn't match clears the field, marks it, and says so out loud. The focus goes straight back.
A code works for ten minutes, once. After five wrong ones, even the right code waits for a new one.
The backend checks only a keyed hash, finds or makes your account, and starts a session in a cookie scripts can't read.
Open any screen without a session, and sign-in opens first. Confirm the code, and you're back where you were going.
Each ride moves the session forward a year. If the backend can't be reached, the screen opens all the same.
Phone to desktop, the six cells keep one calm row.
What the tests prove: the right code signs you in, a wrong one is counted, and a session lasts a year from its last use.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
